hero.title: Copy on one device.
hero.description: Privacy-first clipboard sync across your devices. Text, images and files flow securely — same Wi-Fi or across the internet.

features.title: Feels like the OS clipboard — but cross-platform, searchable, auditable.

h1.title: Use the ⌘C / ⌘V you already know.
h1.lede: No app to open, no file to send, no account to log into. Copy on one device, paste on another — that's it.
h1.b1Desc: An extension of the system clipboard — not another app to switch to.
h1.b2Desc: ⌘C / Ctrl-C to copy, ⌘V / Ctrl-V to paste — no muscle-memory taxes.
h1.b3Desc: Reconnects automatically after Wi-Fi switches and sleep/wake. No re-pairing.

h2.title: The relay only sees ciphertext.
h2.lede: Content is encrypted at the source and decrypted only on your devices. Keys live in the system keyring and never leave your machine.
h2.b1Desc: XChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD — encrypted in transit and at rest.
h2.b2Desc: No email, no phone number — just two devices exchanging a public key.
h2.b3Desc: Open source (AGPL-3.0). Read and verify the crypto yourself.

h3.title: Not just LAN. Not bound to one network.
h3.lede: First-class on Windows, macOS, and Linux. Direct on the same Wi-Fi; NAT hole-punching across networks; encrypted relay as a fallback.
h3.b1Desc: Not an Electron wrapper — built on Rust + Tauri.
h3.b2Desc: Devices on the same network connect peer-to-peer, no relay.
h3.b3Desc: Across home/office/internet — automatic hole-punching, encrypted relay if it fails.

more.f1Desc: First-class support on Windows, macOS, and Linux — your clipboard works wherever you do.
more.f4Desc: Search the full history in milliseconds — even with tens of thousands of entries. The index stays encrypted on disk.
more.f6Desc: A keyboard-shortcut overlay with inline preview for text, links, images, code, and files — feels like part of the OS clipboard.
more.f5Desc: Copy on one device, paste on another. Large files use streaming transfer so they never have to fit in memory.
more.f7Desc: A uniclip CLI mirrors the GUI flow and works headlessly — built for terminals, SSH, scripts, and tmux workflows.
more.f9Desc: Manage paired devices, presence and per-device sync preferences. Lost a device? Revoke it from any paired one.

howItWorks.title: Pair once. After that, just copy and paste.
howItWorks.step1Desc: Devices exchange a public key once, locally — no cloud account, no email. Generate a short-lived invitation code on one device; the new device joins with the code and the space passphrase.
howItWorks.step2Desc: Content is encrypted at the source. Ciphertext flows over a direct P2P link (same Wi-Fi or NAT hole-punching). When direct fails, it falls back to an encrypted relay. Even a malicious relay only sees ciphertext.
howItWorks.step3Desc: Decryption happens only on your devices. Local history and the search index are encrypted at rest. Connections recover automatically after Wi-Fi switches, sleep/wake, or brief disconnects.

item1.q: Why not just iCloud Universal Clipboard?
item1.a: If you only use Apple devices, don't need history, and fully trust Apple's closed-source E2E encryption — iCloud is fine. The moment you add a Windows or Linux machine, want a searchable history, or want to verify the encryption yourself, you need something else.

item2.q: Why not a self-hosted clipboard sync (e.g. ClipCascade)?
item2.a: Self-hosted means you operate a server. UniClipboard works out of the box — direct P2P first, encrypted relay only as a fallback. You never have to run any infrastructure.

item3.q: Does it work fully offline / LAN-only?
item3.a: Yes. Devices on the same Wi-Fi connect directly without going through the relay. Even if the relay is unreachable, devices on the same network keep syncing.

item4.q: Where does my clipboard history actually live?
item4.a: Only on your devices. Local storage is encrypted at rest with a key that never leaves the system keyring. No UniClipboard server ever receives or stores your clipboard content.

item5.a: Not yet. The current release focuses on getting Windows, macOS and Linux right. Mobile is on the roadmap, but OS-level clipboard permissions and background-execution limits need to be solved first — we'll ship it when it's ready, not before.

footer.thanksDesc: Cross-device clipboard sync — end-to-end encrypted, open source, auditable. Flows seamlessly between your own machines, without any cloud account in between.
